text.p: These were the main headlines from Lithuania's M-1 plus radio station's news report on Wednesday afternoon. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Deputy Chairman of Parliament Feliksas Palubinskas said the government does not have a strategic plan and asked parliament to pass a law to order the government and government institutions to plan their activities 10 years in advance.
- A Lithuanian and Polish parliamentary assembly, founded at the end of June, starts a session today in Vilnius. The assembly is expected to elect its leaders and approve a work plan.
- President Algirdas Brazauskas promised that the amount of money the state gives to Lithuanian communities abroad will increase when the Lithuanian economy improves.
- Foreign Minister Algirdas Saudargas will participate in the sixth session of the Council of the Baltic Sea States in Riga on Wednesday and Thursday.
